title: 3d Ai Modeling software with normal triangle/poly count?
author: designhelp123
selftext:
So every time I try creating some 3d model based on a photo or from a prompt, the triangle or poly count is like 100,000, which is obviously not optimal for gaming.

Any recommendations here?

comments.author: justifun
comments.body: Hunyuan 3d has a retopology feature that will make a nicer end result.  Or you have to use a tool like instant mesh to simplifier to a cleaner result.  Or worst case, by hand.

replies.author: OfficeMagic1
replies.body: Just googled and looks like it came out anout a week ago.  Worth checking out?

replies.author: designhelp123
replies.body: I've seen tutorials on this, it seems quite intense, or does Blender have any 'auto-retopologize' options now?

replies.author: Cautious_Cry3928
replies.body:
There are plugins like retopoflow, or the absolute workhorse Quadrrmesher that speed things up.

I think it's worth learning to retopologize at the very least if you're using AI assets, it has to be done whether or not you use AI and is an essential skill. I chose to do a low poly game knowing it would be a million times quicker to retopo everything. If I chose high poly, each character would be a huge challenge.

replies.author: superkickstart
replies.body: It does but you could also try the quad remesh addon. Works fine for most static models but if yoi want good topology for animation or something detailed, its not really possible to fully automate it (yet).

comments.author: pierukainen
comments.body: Rodin lets you choose the polygon count. But the results aren't that good with low count. It's better to let it generate with 100k and fix it in Blender.

replies.author: designhelp123
replies.body: I've used Rodin and the results were quite good. What kind of "fixing" do you recommend within Blender? I'd love to research more.

replies.author: pierukainen
replies.body:
Yes I like Rodin too, but lowpoly stuff hasn't worked too good for me. Polygons are wasted on senseless details while at the same time there are holes etc.

Blender has tools for automatically reducing the polycount. Obviously you get better result if you do it at least partly by hand.

I am still trying to find the most practical approach. Doing it just for a hobby project.

replies.author: designhelp123
replies.body: Same here, trying to build my first game after learning so much about programming in the past year. Seems like Blender is a necessity, so I'll just start generating some models and seeing how the auto-poly-reduction works within the software. Thanks!

replies.author: pierukainen
replies.body: It's really simple actually and Blender is free.

comments.author: KatetCadet
comments.body:
I’ve been doing some discovery around AI for 3d modeling, just is not there yet for gaming.

It works when you can bake animations and want something quick, but it definitely doesn’t work for games IMO.

It sucks at hard surface modeling, can’t get sharp edges and corners with an excessive about of tris. And because of that things like characters with a pouch also end up looking super melted and messy.

The time it takes to fix the topology or make a low poly version is so big you might as well not use AI in the first place.

That being said it can be used for ideation, blocking, etc. Just all the major tools I’ve tried all fail and producing ready to use or even near ready to use assets.

comments.author: OurPillowGuy
comments.body: Have you tried learning how to 3D model?

replies.author: No_Drive2275
replies.body: Lol bro no, life is tho short!

replies.author: Bamzooki1
replies.body: You’d save more time by learning.

replies.author: No_Drive2275
replies.body: AI is almost there, depends on priorities you should try 3d-agent or blender-mcp :)

comments.author: spacespacespapce
comments.body:
[NativeBlend](https://nativeblend.app/discover) is good for this, since it makes models using blender tools instead of spitting out a mesh that you then have to clean up. 

  
(Downside is that it takes a bit longer to generate each model)

comments.body: Take a look on what I have been building, cursor for Blender [3d-agent.com](http://3d-agent.com)

comments.author: Wrong_Spinach_4972
comments.body: I’ve been using Hitem3D because the geometry comes out clean. It produces a usable base mesh rather than a random soup of polygons, which makes manual retopology much faster. It’s not game-ready, but the structure is definitely decent to work from.
